description:
Programme or Project Overview

The University of Amsterdam invites applications for a PhD candidate in systemic actors and the enforcement of digital rules. The project studies how the enforcement of European digital regulation, including the Digital Services Act and the GDPR, is organised across systemic actors such as platforms, regulators, civil society and auditors, and what makes enforcement effective and accountable.

The candidate will analyse legal frameworks and governance practice, conduct empirical research on enforcement interactions, and contribute to academic and public debates on digital regulation. The position is embedded in the university's strong interdisciplinary environment for law and digital society research, and is a salaried four-year PhD track under the CAO-NU collective agreement with a gross monthly salary between EUR 3,204 and EUR 4,051.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a research master's degree in law, governance, social sciences or a related field, with an interest in European digital regulation. Strong analytical writing skills in English are required; empirical-research skills are an advantage. The supervisory team spans law and interdisciplinary digital-society research.

Highlights

  • Enforcement of the DSA, GDPR and related digital rules
  • Systemic actors: platforms, regulators, auditors, civil society
  • Accountability and effectiveness of digital governance
  • Legal-doctrinal and empirical analysis
  • European digital-regulation research networks
  • Salaried PhD, EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month (CAO-NU scale)

About University of Amsterdam

The University of Amsterdam (UvA) is the largest university in the Netherlands and one of Europe's leading research institutions. Its seven faculties span the humanities, social and behavioural sciences, economics and business, law, science, medicine in cooperation with Amsterdam UMC, and dentistry. PhD candidates at the UvA are employed on salaried contracts under the CAO-NU collective agreement, making doctoral research here fully funded. Academic vacancies and doctoral positions are published on the university's academic careers portal with detailed role profiles and application requirements.
